sentences.text:
Shivam Mehrotra @ Shivam Malhotra vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.
Secy. Home Lko. on 21 April, 2023

Author: Rajeev Singh
Bench: Rajeev Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 11
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 3406 of 2022
Applicant :- Shivam Mehrotra @ Shivam Malhotra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru.Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ayodhya Prasad Mishra A.P. Mishra,Rituraj Mishra,Shesh Ram Verm Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ankit Kumar Singh Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
Heard Shri A.P. Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant, Ran Vijay Singh, learned A.G.A for the State of U.P., Shri Harsh Kumar Thaper, learned counsel for the informant and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime/FIR No.271 of 2021, under Section 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Hazratganj,
District-Lucknow, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
The submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is an innocent person and he is in jail since 03.09.2021.
He further submitted that applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case as he was working in the Forest Department and main accused was Anand Singh.
He further submitted that charge-sheet has been filed and there is no possibility of tampering of any evidence.
He further submitted that applicant is ready to cooperate in the trial.

He further submitted Shivam Mehrotra @ Shivam Malhotra vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin. Secy. Home Lko. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113618224/
1

entities.text: Shivam Mehrotra @ Shivam Malhotra vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that alleged offences are triable by Magistrate.
In these circumstances, the applicant is entitled for bail.
In case of being enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 have opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that huge amount was found in the account of applicant,
which was collected from the opposite party No.2/informant as well as others in the name of providing employment in the Forest Department and it is admitted by the co-accused, namely,
Anand Singh that the alleged amount was transferred in the account of applicant, therefore,
applicant is not entitled for bail.

Learned counsel for the opposite party No.2/informant submitted that there is evidence in the statement of account of applicant as well as co-accused-Anand Singh that more than Rs.70 lakhs was found in the account of applicant as well as other accused persons and they cheated in the name of giving employment to the informant and others by way of forged appointment letter.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and going through the contents of FIR, counter affidavit as well as other relevant documents, I find no good ground to grant of bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, the bail application is hereby rejected.
Trial Court is directed to conclude the trial of the present case, expeditiously without granting unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
Office is directed to communicate this order to the authority concerned, forthwith.

Order Date :- 21.4.2023 Amit/-
